assessments.reasoning: The operative Go 1.23 range rule gives each iteration its own variables when the clause declares them with :=. The history identifies Go 1.22 as the introduction of that behavior.

challenge.method: Replace := with = and supply existing variables with the same names.
challenge.results: The assignment form writes successive values into the existing variables. The declaration condition is essential even when the loop produces the same sequence of values.

limitations: A range clause assigning to existing variables with = follows the ordinary assignment rule and falls outside the statement.
Effective language semantics matter. Syntax using = and configurations selecting older language semantics are outside the stated condition.
